criteria.criterion: A lifecycle test named retrying_a_retry_carries_the_original_request_redacted passes: A rejected, B ('try again on A') rejected, then 'try again on B'; the third reader brief contains A's original request (redacted) and B's findings. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test lifecycle retrying_a_retry
criteria.evidence: I ran it: 1 passed. The test rejects A and B, then asks 'try again on B'. It asserts that the last reader brief contains '> add a greeting ORIGINAL-CANARY' and FINDING-B-CANARY, and does not contain '> try again on A'. In the code, the original request goes through redactor.redact_all before it replaces attempt.request.

criteria.criterion: In that test A and B have different verdict findings (distinct canaries), and the assertions require B's canary present and A's absent. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test lifecycle retrying_a_retry
criteria.evidence: The first verifier call returns failing_verdict("FINDING-A-CANARY ...") and later calls return failing_verdict("FINDING-B-CANARY ..."). The test asserts brief.contains("FINDING-B-CANARY") and !brief.contains("FINDING-A-CANARY"). It passed.

criteria.criterion: Existing try-again tests still pass, including landed/unknown refusal and plain retry. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test lifecycle try_again
A test covers bare 'try again on' being refused with the 'say which job' message. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-core reading
criteria.evidence: reading::tests::a_bare_try_again_on_is_refused_and_a_named_job_is_found passed. It checks 'try again on', 'Try again on   ' and 'try again on .' for the 'say which job' error. Before the change, 'try again on' with no trailing space was not refused at all; the new exact-match check refuses it.

summary: The change fixes the retry-of-retry bug. When the retried job was itself "try again on <job>", `earlier_attempt` now follows the chain back to the first request that is not a retry, with a cycle guard and a depth limit of 16. It redacts that request and carries it in place of the retry phrase, together with the retried job's own findings. I ran every cited command and all passed: the new lifecycle test, the existing try-again tests, the core `reading` tests (including the new bare-refusal unit test), the reader-brief tests, fmt and clippy. The new test would fail without the fix, because it asserts the retry phrase is absent and the original request is present. CHANGELOG has a `### Fixed` entry after `### Added`, and the review-1 bullet is still under Added. The design doc and the review file are unchanged. `briefs.rs` was listed as a deliverable but was not changed; the fix did not need it. Two small notes: no test feeds a secret through the chain to show redaction directly, and `### Fixed` sits before `### Changed`, which differs from Keep a Changelog's usual section order.
